comment: Recorded aggregates for the fla-npu chunk on Ascend 950DT, backing docs/records/npu-fla-chunk-ascend950dt.md. The raw 60-answer corpus and the golden-check run lived on the measurement host, which is no longer available; this file reconstructs the published aggregates from the record. The rerun tracked in the linked issue supersedes and extends it (per-request table and the npu golden-check entry).

label_diff.notes: One leaf per flipped request (2 prompts x 2 runs, deterministic); every flipped leaf has a two-option probability gap <= 0.02 and leaves with larger margins do not move; the two flip directions are opposite, consistent with a random walk rather than a systematic bias. The two fused implementations (triton-FLA and Ascend C) agree with each other on all 60; the NPU reference implementation agrees with the CUDA production recordings on all 60.

chunk_probe.notes: Single-request d3-mini forward, chunk term isolated by single-point synchronous timing; the chunk term is 97% of the baseline forward.

divergence_probe.per_call_max_abs_diff_note: 2^-8, the reported BF16 GDN rounding floor (arxiv 2609.04098); single-call divergence does not grow with sequence length (T=200..500 all <= 3.9e-3)
divergence_probe.fp64_truth_max_ulp_note: both implementations sit at max 1 ulp from the fp64 reference: two equally-correct rounding paths, not a wrong kernel

g_distribution_probe.notes: The measured d3-mini decay range; why the CANN ops-transformer chunk_gated_delta_rule (hard constraint g in [-1, 0]) cannot serve this model, and why clamping would break long-range forgetting.

gates.consent: 93.3% row agreement < the 99% bar: the released BF16 d3 packages keep exact kernels; the slot lands default-off behind the FLA_NPU_APPROXIMATE opt-in, to flip only when the quantized d3 accuracy record lands
